jobs.title: New Business Consultant
jobs.description: What You'll Do The New Business Consultant is instrumental to the success of regional sales offices by building partnerships with our financial professionals, accurately onboarding new client accounts, managing account openings and asset movement requests with broker-dealer, and serving as a point of contact between financial professionals, product partners, and custodians. Here are a few examples of the kinds of things you’ll do: Provide training to financial professionals for new business protocols and technology fundamentals. Assist in the onboarding of new clients by accurately preparing and processing insurance, annuity, and investment account applications. Manage account openings and asset movement requests with broker dealer. Utilize industry technology, such as Salesforce CRM and proprietary product platforms to create, track, manage, and complete tasks related to new business operations. Implement and manage systems to track multiple time sensitive deadlines and maintain electronic client files. Communicate new account statuses, resolve client service issues, and support financial professional-client relationships through regular follow-ups. Assist with routine account or policy maintenance items for both new and existing clients and serve as a point of contact between the financial professional, product partners and custodians. Perform other job-related duties or projects as needed, which may include administrative tasks such as greeting guests, managing mail, answering phones, ordering supplies, and facilities management. Adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements while performing work activities and follow high standards of business ethics in all client interactions and transactions. Operating at the intersection of financial services and technology, Principal builds financial tools that help our customers live better lives. We take pride in being a purpose-led firm, motivated by our mission to make financial security accessible to all. Our mission, integrity, and customer focus have made us a trusted leader for more than 140 years! Who You Are Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in finance, business administration, or a related field preferred. 2+ years of related work experience in life insurance/broker-dealer or RIA operations: client service, account opening, account management, or operations. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with industry-specific software and CRM systems. Ability to quickly learn new web-based programs. Understanding of basic financial terms, products, services, regulations, and compliance standards. Strong customer service, organization, critical thinking, and ability to learn new skills required. Experience with Salesforce and/or other CRM platforms is highly preferred. A keen sense of urgency and responsiveness to customer needs as well as communication and relationship building skills. Ability to prioritize assignments, adapt to changing priorities and perform under pressure. Familiarity with FINRA regulations preferred. jobs.title: Corporate Strategy & Development Director
jobs.description: What You'll Do We’re looking for a Corporate Strategy & Development Director to join our Corporate Strategy and Development team. In this role, you will lead complex strategy and transaction initiatives that contribute to Principal’s long-term growth, profitability, and competitive position. This role will work flexibly across a broad range of enterprise and business-unit priorities, including mergers and acquisitions. Assignments may span different businesses, geographies, and strategic questions, requiring the ability to quickly orient to new subject matter, create structure in ambiguous situations, and drive work toward clear decisions and outcomes. You will work closely with enterprise and business-unit senior leaders to evaluate strategic opportunities, develop fact-based recommendations, translate strategic ideas into actionable plans, and drive disciplined execution. The successful candidate will combine strong financial and analytical capabilities with strategic judgment, intellectual agility, adaptability, collaborative leadership, and a high degree of ownership. You’ll have the opportunity to: Develop clear, fact-based strategic and financial recommendations for senior management regarding growth opportunities, portfolio priorities, capital deployment, business performance, and other enterprise-level decisions. Structure and lead complex projects by defining the key questions, analytical approach, workplan, roles, and decision points required to move the work forward. Lead mergers, acquisitions, dispositions, strategic partnerships, financing transactions, and other capital-related initiatives across Principal’s businesses and geographies. Manage transactions throughout the full lifecycle, including strategic assessment, financial analysis, valuation, due diligence, transaction structuring, negotiation, governance and approval processes, signing, closing, and transition planning. Identify, evaluate, and advance inorganic growth and portfolio-management opportunities in partnership with business leaders, strategists, finance professionals, functional experts, and external advisors. Lead cross-functional teams, maintain momentum across multiple workstreams, identify and resolve execution risks, and drive initiatives toward timely decisions and outcomes. Quickly develop a strong understanding of unfamiliar businesses, markets, geographies and transaction structures and translate that understanding into actionable insights and recommendations. Build productive relationships with potential buyers, sellers, strategic partners, investment bankers, consultants, legal advisors, and other external counterparties. Work effectively across different businesses, functions, geographies, and cultures, including on matters involving international teams, partners, advisors, and counterparties. Provide strategic planning and problem-solving support to business units, including market assessment, competitive analysis, performance improvement, benchmarking, organizational design, and implementation planning. Serve as a trusted thought partner to senior leaders while remaining actively involved in the detailed analysis, coordination, and execution required to move initiatives forward. Communicate complex strategic, financial, and transaction-related matters clearly and effectively to senior executives, governance bodies, business partners, and external stakeholders. Coach, develop, and provide oversight to junior members of the Corporate Strategy and Development team. Perform other strategic initiatives and special projects as required. Operating at the intersection of financial services and technology, Principal builds financial tools that help our customers live better lives. We take pride in being a purpose-led firm, motivated by our mission to make financial security accessible to all. Our mission, integrity, and customer focus have made us a trusted leader for more than 140 years. Who You Are Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, actuarial science, or a related field, with eight or more years of relevant professional experience. Significant experience in corporate development, investment banking, private equity, transaction advisory, strategic finance, management consulting, or a comparable transaction- or strategy-oriented role. Demonstrated M&A experience, including financial analysis and valuation, due diligence, transaction structuring, negotiation, stakeholder management, and transaction execution. Strong financial acumen, including the ability to evaluate financial statements, business models, valuation analyses, capital structures, and the economic implications of strategic alternatives. Demonstrated ability to take ownership of complex initiatives, establish structure in ambiguous situations, manage multiple priorities, and drive work from initial analysis through decision and execution. Ability to move effectively between strategic and long-range thinking and hands-on execution, with strong attention to detail and accountability for results. Strong problem-solving skills and intellectual agility, with the ability to assess new situations quickly, identify the critical issues, and develop practical, well-reasoned solutions. A collaborative, team-oriented leadership style characterized by ownership, adaptability, resilience, sound judgment, humility, and a willingness to contribute wherever needed. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trust and productive working relationships across business units, functions, organizational levels, and cultures. Strong communication, negotiation, and influencing skills, with the executive presence required to work effectively with senior leaders and external counterparties. Ability to communicate directly and constructively, navigate differing perspectives, and create alignment among stakeholders with varied objectives. Broad understanding of the financial services industry, capital markets, and the regulatory, competitive, and economic factors affecting financial-services businesses. Experience working on cross-border matters or with international teams, advisors, and counterparties is preferred. A demonstrated interest in and ability to operate effectively across different markets and cultures is important. MBA, CFA, CPA, or another relevant advanced degree or professional designation is preferred. Additional language capabilities are welcome but are not required. Salary Range Information Salary ranges below reflect targeted base salaries. Non-sales positions have the opportunity to participate in a bonus program. Sales positions are eligible for sales incentives, and in some instances a bonus plan, whereby total compensation may far exceed base salary depending on individual performance. Actual compensation for all roles will be based upon geographic location, work experience, education, licensure requirements and/or skill level and will be finalized at the time of offer. Salary Range (Non-Exempt expressed as hourly; Exempt expressed as yearly) $141000 - $191000 / year Time Off Program Flexible Time Off (FTO) is provided to salaried (exempt) employees and provides the opportunity to take time away from the office with pay for vacation, personal or short-term illness. Employees don’t accrue a bank of time off under FTO and there is no set number of days provided. Pension Eligible Yes Work Environment This role offers in-office, hybrid—blending at least three office days in a typical workweek—and remote work arrangements for individuals residing more than 30 miles from Des Moines, Iowa; Raleigh, North Carolina; or Charlotte, North Carolina. Strong preference for Des Moines, IA based candidates. You’ll work with your leader to determine which option best aligns based on applicable business and individual considerations. jobs.title: Senior Associate, Portfolio Management, Private Equity Real Estate (Data Center Team)
jobs.description: What You'll Do The Senior Associate supports the management and growth of Private Markets Real Estate's data center and digital infrastructure investments. This role combines portfolio management, investment analysis, and asset management responsibilities, partnering closely with acquisitions, development, operations, and asset management teams. The position will support portfolio performance monitoring, investment evaluation, strategic decision-making, and asset oversight across the investment lifecycle. The ideal candidate brings strong analytical skills, data center industry knowledge, and the ability to balance portfolio-level objectives with asset-level execution. Strategy & Investment Analysis Support portfolio strategy and investment decision-making across data center investments. Evaluate acquisitions, developments, financings, and dispositions. Conduct financial, market, and operational analyses to identify risks and opportunities. Prepare investment recommendations and materials for senior leadership and investment committees. Portfolio Management Monitor portfolio performance and support portfolio optimization efforts. Analyze investment results, market trends, and key performance indicators. Develop forecasts, financial models, and performance analyses to support investment decisions. Prepare portfolio reporting, market insights, and materials for internal and external stakeholders. Partner across teams to align investments with portfolio objectives and business plans. Asset Management & Operational Oversight Support asset performance and execution of business plans across the portfolio. Work with operating partners and internal teams to identify value creation opportunities. Monitor financial, operational, and market performance metrics. Assist with strategic decisions related to leasing, development, capital projects, and portfolio growth. Collaboration Collaborate across acquisitions, asset management, research, legal, operations, and capital markets teams to support investment and portfolio objectives. Contribute to investment analyses, presentations, and strategic initiatives through effective partnership and knowledge sharing. Support a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement Who You Are Bachelor's degree in Finance, Real Estate, Economics, Business, Engineering, or a related field. 4+ years of experience in real estate, infrastructure, private markets investing, or asset management. Direct experience supporting or managing data center investments, assets, developments, or operations with a meaningful focus on the sector. Strong financial modeling, investment analysis, and problem-solving capabilities. Understanding of real estate and infrastructure investments, including acquisitions, development, operations, and portfolio management. Effective communicator with the ability to present complex analyses and recommendations to a variety of stakeholders. Self-motivated team player who can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Willingness to travel as needed (5-10%).
